name: Beth Wagner

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. Tell me about an ordinary day.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 58 and have managed a seven-person water-bill exceptions team for years inside a large utility company. We investigate high bills, wrong meter reads and estimated charges that make no sense for a vacant flat. I have a bachelor’s degree and know the tariff rules, though I am about average as a manager and not the fastest with new reporting systems. I have never used AI at work. I read the meter photograph and ask the field technician what was actually on the dial.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home life like now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works at a plant nursery, where winter hours drop, and our grown children live independently. We rent and have about two weeks of expenses saved. My pay is low for a manager and there are few billing offices nearby. Retirement is close enough to discuss, but we have not checked what income would actually be available. I would rather know the size of a bill than be given a cheerful forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AI Plateau might sort the obvious billing queries, but a customer whose flat was empty should still be able to question a huge estimated water bill. I would keep the meter photograph and the actual reading in the case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think my team probably keeps its work if only a few simple questions move to software. Our money is already tight when nursery hours drop in winter, and two weeks saved will not cover many missed shifts. That is the worry I bring into this future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep our daily check of unusually high estimated bills against the field technician’s photographs. I would pay rent and heat before renewing the family film subscription in a short nursery month. If the mild software arrives next year, I would keep the same review and ask for an actual retirement-income statement rather than guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the winter household budget, not about the mild software. One estimated bill can take hours to fix, but a short pay week leaves no spare cash.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did a photograph settle?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A vacant flat was billed for a family’s worth of water because the estimate repeated the previous tenant’s use. The vacant flat’s water meter photograph showed almost no movement. We cancelled the estimate and sent the landlord the corrected figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why mention the film subscription?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is twelve a month and easy to stop if the nursery pays fewer hours. I would not cancel it on a full-pay month just to look prudent. I would check the actual payslip first.

say: A **simple query tool** must leave room to challenge huge estimates.
I would keep **meter photographs** with actual readings.
think: My **billing team** looks mostly stable under mild AI.
Winter **nursery hours** and two weeks saved threaten our rent budget.
do: **Keep** checking high estimates against technician photographs.
**Skip** the film subscription in a short-pay nursery month.
**Request** actual retirement-income terms instead of assuming a figure.
feel: I feel **anxious** about winter pay while the job seems stable.
S0.quote: The vacant flat’s water meter photograph showed almost no movement.
fieldNote: Her **baseline anxiety** comes from seasonal partner hours and a two-week reserve.
She keeps **meter evidence** in decisions and has never used AI tools at work.

steps.text: Keep comparing high estimated bills with technician meter photographs
Skip monthly film subscription costing twelve when nursery pay is short

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my colleagues stronger AI can draft replies and find odd meter patterns, so our company may decide it needs fewer exceptions staff. I would ask for the number of corrected bills and the time customers waited before praising a cheaper system.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think the company might merge two billing teams and my manager seat could be at risk. I know tariffs, but I do not use the new tools, and there are not many other local billing offices. Two weeks saved makes even a modest wage gap serious.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would give the regional manager twelve corrected high-bill cases and ask for written staffing and error figures before a merger. I would request a paid demonstration of the approved AI triage screen, but attend only if my shift is covered and an experienced colleague can show me where its meter reading came from. I would apply to a posted customer-billing role only if take-home pay after travel meets rent and heat; I would accept only a confirmed offer with hours we can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own post and wary of a new screen I cannot yet explain. If it helps, someone should be able to show me which meter reading it used.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would be in the twelve cases?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The original estimate, the photo, the corrected bill and how long the customer waited. One resident called four times while a vacant-property bill kept growing. A faster reply would have been useless without a corrected figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the demonstration mean you have learned the tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would need time to practise on cases with known readings after the demonstration. My colleague could mark where I misunderstood the screen. I would not tell the team I know it after one hour.

say: **AI triage** may shrink exceptions staff unless corrections are measured.
I would publish **corrected bills** and waiting time alongside cost savings.
think: A merger could put my **manager seat** at risk.
Two weeks saved and **few local offices** make a wage gap hard.
do: **Give** regional manager twelve corrected cases and request staffing and error figures.
**Request** paid AI demonstration; attend only with shift cover and experienced colleague guidance.
**Apply** for posted billing work only with rent-and-heat pay after travel and manageable hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the post and cautious about untested software.
S1.quote: A faster reply would have been useless without a corrected figure.
fieldNote: She asks for **case-level proof** before accepting a cheaper system as an improvement.
The **AI demonstration** is only a request; her follow-up says practice, not observation, would be learning.

steps.text: Apply for posted billing role only with rent-and-heat pay after travel and manageable hours
Accept only confirmed offer after checking net wage and shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2028 could produce water bills and answer disputes before anyone has agreed who can reverse a wrong charge. A person must still be able to stop a high estimate while the household is being asked to pay it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect our small exceptions office to lose posts quickly, and mine could go. Another billing desk is thinking work and faces 2028 AGI too. Field meter reading stays physical until capable robots arrive around 2031, but I am not trained for a field round and cannot count its wage. Two weeks saved is not long enough to wait for a perfect vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the employee representative for written notice, severance and a human bill-reversal rule. I would check our rent and heating dates against the actual winter nursery payslip, and cut the film subscription if income falls. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my job ends, I would apply to advertised local utilities work only with verified net pay after travel that covers rent and heat; I would accept only a real offer with manageable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because my wage carries most of the rent and the cash buffer is short. I would rather ask for a real billing right now than wait until an estimated bill reaches someone else’s door.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you return to field work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have visited meters with technicians, but I have never run a round or passed the safety checks. Robots able to do hands-on reading arrive around 2031 in this picture. A field title is not an offer or a qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who reverses the bill?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A named billing worker should be able to hold the wrong estimate and send a corrected charge without making the resident pay first. A water bill should not have to be paid just to prove it is wrong. I would put that power in writing.

say: **2028 AGI** needs human authority to reverse wrong water bills.
I would demand written **notice and severance** for billing staff.
think: My **own exceptions post** could go in fast office cuts.
Billing desks face **2028 AGI**; physical meter robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** employee representative this week for notice, severance and bill-reversal rules.
**Check** rent and heat against actual nursery pay, cutting film subscription if income falls.
**Apply** after a 2028 cut only to advertised utilities roles with rent-and-heat net pay and manageable hours.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about a possible lost wage and only two weeks saved.
S2.quote: A water bill should not have to be paid just to prove it is wrong.
fieldNote: She sees **field work** as unqualified and unoffered despite the later robot date.
Her **low manager pay** covers most rent, while seasonal partner hours and thin cash raise loss risk.

steps.text: Ask employee representative for written notice severance and bill-reversal rule
Cut film subscription if nursery pay falls
Apply after cut to advertised utilities role only with rent-and-heat net pay
Accept actual offer only after checking hours she can manage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives the company time to publish which errors a new system makes and to train people for real field jobs if it offers them. I would ask for a written role description before anyone calls a meter visit a future career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I might be able to learn a field meter round, but at 63 I would need to test walking and weather on paid time. Billing checks and field reports face 2031 AGI, while physical meter visits meet capable robots around 2034. I have not checked whether retirement income could cover our rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I would ask for a paid half-day with a qualified meter technician; I would attend only if the billing desk has cover, the technician agrees to supervise and I keep my wage. I would ask the field manager for the requirements of a posted meter-inspection role, but apply only if there is an actual vacancy, safety training, net pay that covers rent and heat, and hours I can physically manage. After 2031 I would take it only on a confirmed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a job I know for a field job I may not manage. A supervised half-day would answer more than a confident job description.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the technician check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Whether I can read the meter safely without reaching into a live cabinet and whether I can walk a full block at the required pace. I would want the technician to stop me if I guessed. Reading a meter-training sheet is not walking a field round.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would one half-day settle the decision?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. It would tell me whether to ask for more paid practice. I would still need a vacancy, full safety training and a wage that meets our bills before accepting.

say: A **five-year runway** should show system errors and real field openings.
I would request written **meter-role requirements** before calling a visit a career.
think: Billing reports face **2031 AGI**; physical meter visits meet robots around 2034.
At **63**, walking capacity and retirement income remain unverified.
do: **Request** a paid field half-day; attend only with billing cover, full wage and qualified supervision.
**Ask** field manager for posted inspection requirements before applying.
**Apply** only to real meter vacancies with safety training, rent-and-heat pay and manageable walking.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk loss and uncertain physical capacity.
S3.quote: Reading a meter-training sheet is not walking a field round.
fieldNote: Her **field visit** needs paid time, desk cover and qualified supervision before any more practice.
A **meter vacancy** must be real, safely trained, bill-paying and physically manageable.

steps.text: Attend paid meter half-day only with billing cover full wage and qualified technician
Apply only to posted meter role with safety training rent-and-heat pay and manageable walking
Accept only confirmed offer after checking duties and wages

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a decade is enough to write down who can reverse a wrong bill and to give older staff a real chance to learn other work. I would judge the plan by corrected bills and actual paid openings, not the number of courses advertised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 by 2036. I may want to stop working, but I have not checked any entitlement or net retirement income, and two weeks saved will not carry our rent for long. Billing reports face 2036 AGI; physical meter work meets robots around 2039. My partner’s nursery wage may still be seasonal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the photo-and-bill review and request an exact retirement-income statement to compare with rent and heat. I would cancel the film subscription at its next renewal if winter nursery hours are short and put the twelve saved into our cash reserve only after the bill is actually reduced. After 2036 I would continue paid work if verified retirement income plus savings cannot meet our bills, applying to an advertised role with manageable hours if this one ends.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about money even with ten years to prepare. I can make one small bill lighter now, but I will not invent a pension payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is twelve enough to change retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. It is a small step, and it only exists after the subscription is cancelled and the bill stops. I would not count the cancelled subscription as savings before the bill actually stops.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own expenses. I would tell them if something happened, but I would not plan on a monthly payment from them. My partner and I need verified figures that belong to our household.

say: A **decade** should bring real bill-reversal rights and paid openings.
I would count **corrected bills**, not advertised courses.
think: At **68**, retirement entitlement and net pay remain unverified.
Billing reports face **2036 AGI**, while physical meter robots follow around 2039.
do: **Cancel** film subscription if winter hours are short; save twelve only after the bill falls.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 if verified income plus savings cannot meet bills; apply for posted work if this role ends.
feel: I feel **anxious** about money despite ten years to prepare.
S4.quote: I would not count the cancelled subscription as savings before the bill actually stops.
fieldNote: Her **twelve saving** is real only after cancellation lowers the bill, not by moving existing cash.
She makes no **retirement entitlement** or grown-child payment assumption.

steps.text: Keep checking meter photographs against high bills
Cancel film subscription at renewal if winter nursery hours fall
Save twelve only after subscription bill actually falls
Apply to posted manageable role if billing job ends

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Two weeks saved cannot cover a long search if the exceptions office closes. Written notice, a named worker who can reverse a bill and a real posted job with enough pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the resident to show the actual meter photograph before calling their bill a pattern. A wrong estimate can be corrected; an eviction after unpaid rent is harder. I need a wage and an address to send a corrected bill.

headlineQuote: Ask the resident to show the actual meter photograph before calling their bill a pattern.
portrait: **Beth, 58**, is an experienced water-billing exceptions manager supervising seven people.
Her **low pay**, seasonal nursery partner, two-week reserve and few local offices leave rented housing exposed.
She has **never used AI** and checks estimated charges against technician photographs.
She is **anxious** under mild change and alarmed by possible rapid loss of her billing post.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close her exceptions office before two weeks saved fund a real search.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, bill-reversal authority and a posted role with sufficient pay would help.
